title: Derived coinduction adjunction and scalar evaluation comparison
statement:
Let $P\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $U:D(A)\to D(P)$ be restriction of scalars in the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $Y\in D(P)$, let $C(Y)\in D(A)$ be derived coinduction: a K-injective representative $I$ of $Y$ gives $C(Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,I)$ with $(a\cdot h)(a')=h(a'a)$; its restriction is $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,Y)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every $X\in D(A)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(P)$
$$\Theta_{X,Y}:U R\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,C(Y))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_P(UX,Y).$$
It is induced on Hom complexes by evaluation at $1$, $f\mapsto(x\mapsto f(x)(1))$, with inverse $g\mapsto(x\mapsto[a\mapsto g(ax)])$. Put $D=C(P[0])$ and let $n\in\mathbf Z$. Under $\Theta_{D[n],P[n]}$ and the canonical shift identifications, the scalar-action morphism $A[0]\to U R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D[n],D[n])$ becomes the canonical double-dual evaluation morphism $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P),P)$. In the Hom-complex model, this compatibility is evaluation $a\mapsto(h\mapsto h(a))$. No perfectness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71 (derived coinduction adjunction and evaluation counit), and Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, displayed double-Hom calculation in the proof of (1)(c).

proof.text: Choose a K-injective $P$-complex $I$ representing $Y$ and an $A$-complex $E$ representing $X$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], on the one-object identity-cover site. Apply [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model]: $J=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(A[0],I)$ is K-injective over $A$, represents $C(Y)$, and evaluation at $1$ gives the chain isomorphism $T$ with the stated inverse. Thus the two complexes compute the two derived Homs by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Localizing $T$ gives $\Theta_{X,Y}$.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext): K-injective coinduction model; explicit total-Hom transposition and null-homotopy argument expanded from these, with derived.tex Tag 070H (definition-K-injective).

proof.text: This is independent of representatives and natural in both derived variables. The model lemma gives precomposition and postcomposition naturality, including homotopies. By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], source quasi-isomorphisms and quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective targets induce quasi-isomorphisms of Hom complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], derived maps between K-injective representatives are chain maps uniquely up to homotopy. Coinduction carries these homotopies to homotopies by the model lemma. These naturality identities therefore descend through localization, whose universal property is [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and through the canonical resolution comparisons. This gives the asserted natural isomorphism, with its prescribed formulas.

Now take $I$ representing $P[0]$ and $V=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(A[0],I)$. By [lem-trf-coinduction-shift-scalar-model], $C(P[n])$ is represented by $V[n]$, the simultaneous-shift comparison commutes with $T$, and it takes scalar multiplication on $V[n]$ exactly to $\delta_I(a)(h)=h(a)$. Its degree-zero sign is one, so this is an equality of chain maps for every integer $n$. Apply [lem-trf-degree-zero-derived-bidual-model] with $M=UA$: the localization of this same $\delta_I$ is the canonical coefficient-bidual morphism, with precisely the K-injective Hom identifications used above. Therefore the scalar-action morphism becomes canonical double-dual evaluation under $\Theta_{D[n],P[n]}$ and shift cancellation, as required.
